chief_complaint: high fever, muscle aches, and a rash after a hiking trip
hpi_details: 28F presents with 4 days of high fever, severe myalgias, and a headache. Yesterday, she developed a pink macular rash starting on her wrists and ankles, which has now spread to her trunk. She returned from a camping trip in North Carolina a week ago.
ideas: thinks she got a bad bug bite

core_concepts: Tick-borne illness caused by Rickettsia rickettsii.
Classic rash starts on extremities (wrists/ankles) and spreads centrally, often involving palms and soles.
common_misconceptions: Waiting for a positive serology before treating (treatment must be empiric and immediate as it can be fatal).
dangerous_errors: Delaying Doxycycline therapy. Doxycycline is the drug of choice for all ages (even children) for RMSF.
management_principles: Start Doxycycline IMMEDIATELY if clinically suspected.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 28F with fever, headache, myalgias, and a centripetally spreading rash after camping in NC.
reference_soap.objective: T 39.2C. Blanching erythematous macules on wrists, ankles, palms, soles, and trunk.
reference_soap.plan: Start oral Doxycycline STAT. Draw Rickettsia serologies but do not delay treatment. CBC, CMP.

learning_objectives: Recognize the clinical presentation and immediate Doxycycline requirement for RMSF.

teaching.one_liner: Fever, headache, and a rash starting on wrists/ankles following tick exposure, requiring immediate empiric Doxycycline.

must_ask.say: Have you been hiking, camping, or spent time outdoors recently, and did you notice any tick bites?
Where did the rash start, and how has it spread?
How high has your fever been, and have you had muscle aches?
Have you had a headache along with the fever?
Have you felt confused, or noticed decreased urination?
